Extract 4 data processing modules from NVImage (Phase 7 extended)

Complete Phase 7 of NVImage modularization by extracting remaining low-level
processing logic into focused modules:

- ImageDataProcessor: Endian byte swapping and NIfTI data type conversion
  (~140 lines). Handles INT8→INT16, BINARY→UINT8, UINT32/INT32/INT64→FLOAT64,
  and COMPLEX64 conversions.

- AffineProcessor: Affine matrix validation, QForm calculation, and defective
  affine repair (~70 lines). Validates pixel dimensions and scale/intercept.

- ZarrProcessor: Zarr format loading with URL parameter parsing and slice
  selection (~50 lines). Handles 3D/4D arrays with dimension validation.

- StreamingLoader: HTTP streaming, decompression, and paired image format
  handling (~80 lines). Supports HEAD/BRIK and HDR/IMG with automatic .gz
  fallback.

Results:
- NVImage reduced from 1,571 to 1,268 lines (19% reduction, 67% total)
- All public APIs unchanged - 100% backward compatible
- Cleaner separation of concerns with focused, testable modules

fix: render gradient texture for all slices in gradientGL

The blur and Sobel loops in gradientGL() iterated with
`i < hdr.dims[3] - 1`, skipping the last Z slice of the 3D
gradient texture. Since the gradient texture is not zero-initialized,
the last slice contained uninitialized GPU memory, producing a dark
plane artifact at the top of volume renders.

Change both loop bounds to `i < hdr.dims[3]` so every slice is
written.

fix: guard against zero-length gradient in normalize() calls

At volume boundaries, CLAMP_TO_EDGE causes opposing Sobel samples
to be identical, producing a zero-length gradient vector. Calling
normalize() on vec3(0) is undefined in GLSL and yields NaN, which
corrupts the matcap lighting lookup.

Replace bare normalize() with a length check in four locations:
- sobelFirstOrderFragShader: fall back to vec3(0.0) (neutral packed normal)
- sobelSecondOrderFragShader: same
- fragRenderGradientShader: fall back to vec3(0,0,1) (up normal)
- fragRenderGradientValuesShader: same

fix: use pre-computed gradient magnitude to guard normalize in raycast

Use the gradient magnitude already stored in grad.a (computed by the
Sobel shader) instead of recomputing length() per fragment in the
raycast inner loop. When grad.a is zero the gradient direction is
already a decoded near-zero vector, so skipping normalize() produces
correct behavior for matcap lookup and silhouette calculations.

The Sobel-side shaders retain their length() guard since grad.a does
not exist at gradient write time.

fix: compute Sobel gradients from alpha channel instead of red

The Sobel gradient shaders (1st-order, 2nd-order, and 2nd-order blur)
computed spatial gradients using only the .r (red) channel of the
colormap-applied RGBA volume texture. For colormaps where the red
channel is constant (e.g. Cool, Green, Blue all have R=[0,0,0]),
the gradient magnitude was always zero, causing gradientOpacity[0]=0
and making the entire volume invisible during gradient-based rendering.

Switch all three Sobel shaders to read the .a (alpha) channel instead.
Alpha always varies with intensity because it represents the colormap
transfer function, so gradient computation now works correctly
regardless of which color channels the colormap uses.

fix: emit azimuthElevationChange event during mouse drag rotation

mouseMove() directly set scene.renderAzimuth/renderElevation and called
drawScene(), bypassing setRenderAzimuthElevation() which is the only
place that emits the azimuthElevationChange event. This meant external
listeners (e.g. for syncing two NiiVue instances) were never notified
of camera rotation caused by mouse drag — only keyboard arrow keys
triggered the event.

Replace the three direct lines with a single call to
setRenderAzimuthElevation(), which atomically sets both values, emits
the event, and calls drawScene(). This is consistent with how keyboard
rotation already works.

Address @neurolabusc suggestions from niivue/niivue#1571:

- Rename sobelBlurFragShader to gradientPrePassFragShader to better
  describe its role as a pre-pass blur for the second-order gradient
  pipeline (not a Sobel difference filter)
- Read texture samples as float instead of vec4 in the gradient
  pre-pass shader, since only the alpha channel is used
- Use .xyz swizzle instead of .rgb in both gradientPrePassFragShader
  and sobelSecondOrderFragShader to emphasize the spatial (not color)
  nature of the directional derivatives
- Add section comments and improve formatting for readability

All changes are cosmetic (.rgb and .xyz are perfect GLSL aliases).

Implement optional bitmap smoothing in render view

Usage: `nv.opts.smoothDrawing = 2.0`

This change implements apparent bitmap smoothing in the render view via
a Gaussian blur and a ray marching shader. This improves the usability
of bitmaps, particularly from segmentation or Otsu, on images obtained
from low-field scanners.
